items.evidence: customer-note.spec.ts:92-93 reloads the page and asserts the note field holds the new value. That would fail if the customerUpdate mutation never ran.
All three criteria are covered: actor 'customer' (user.manager) at :74, the value after saving at :88, and the value after a reload at :92-93.

No existing page object covers the customer details screen, so CustomerPage is new rather than a copy. findCustomerId reuses gql/adminToken from lib/graphql.ts and the CUSTOMER constant instead of duplicating them.
No hard waits. customerPage.ts:31 waits on a web-first toBeDisabled assertion.
The spec uses test from fixtures/test.ts and is not tagged parallel(). It writes nothing to the cache and changes no seed state.
All locators are data-test-ids that exist in src (customer-details, customer-note, button-bar-confirm), and the note input is scoped to the details card.
The orders scenario supplies the customer. The spec only reads its id through the API and makes the note change as the action under test.
No hard-coded ids. The customer is looked up by the scenario's CUSTOMER.email.
Signs in through the stored session with test.use({ actor: "customer" }), the single-permission customer-management user. There is no UI login and no credentials in the spec.
typecheck.txt reports 'exit 0: no errors', and the spec is under e2e/tests/customers/.
The spec only calls CustomerPage methods and asserts on its locators.
customerPage.ts:11-17 uses readonly fields initialised from this.page and constructor(readonly page: Page) {}.
Has // Arrange and // Act & Assert comments (spec :79, :85).
One test for one story, with a test.step for each stage (:86, :91).
The title describes the behaviour and carries the #e2e tag (:78).
A header comment at :69-73 says what the spec covers and why.
Uses web-first toHaveValue and toBeDisabled assertions.
Imports ORDERS_SCENARIO and CUSTOMER rather than typing them as literals. The note string is the test's own input, not a scenario value.
No cleanup steps and no unique or random names.
No custom timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.
Relative imports keep the .ts extension. The spec takes test and expect only from the fixture; the page object imports expect from @playwright/test, as homePage.ts and draftOrderPage.ts do.
The gql call is typed (gql<{ user: { id: string } | null }>), with no any or casts.
The comments explain reasons, such as why saveNote waits for the save button to disable, rather than narrating the code.

It adds a CustomerPage page object, a findCustomerId read helper alongside findOrderId in the orders scenario, and one spec. The spec runs as the customer-management actor on the orders scenario. It saves a note, checks the field, then reloads and checks the note is still there, which proves the save reached the server. Locators are scoped data-test-ids, there are no hard waits, and the type check passes.
